title: Carrier Mobility Explorer
description: Two log-log plots of electron or hole mobility in silicon, against temperature (50-600 K) and against ionized impurity concentration (1e14-1e19 cm^-3), with a partial mobility curve for each scattering mechanism and the Matthiessen total. Checkboxes switch mechanisms on and off, and a readout strip shows each mechanism's share of the total scattering.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: semiconductor physics
carrier mobility
scattering mechanisms
Matthiessen's rule
ionized impurity scattering
phonon scattering

educational.topic: Temperature and doping dependence of carrier mobility in silicon
learningObjectives: Identify which scattering mechanism dominates at a given temperature and doping
Use Matthiessen's rule to combine partial mobilities
Predict how a change in temperature or doping changes the net mobility
prerequisites: Drift velocity and the definition of mobility

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter sliders and mechanism toggles with real-time log-log plots and a probe readout
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Predict-test-observe: students predict the dominant mechanism at a probe point, then check the scattering shares
assessmentOpportunities: Add reciprocal partial mobilities by hand and compare with the displayed total
Predict the dominant mechanism at three temperature and doping combinations
Explain the mobility peak on the temperature plot

equations: mu_op, mu_iv ~ T^-0.5 (exp(theta/T) - 1), theta = 731 K (holes), 630 K (electrons)
assumptions: Electrons: mu_min = 65, mu_0 = 1330 cm^2/V.s, N_ref = 1.26e17 cm^-3, alpha = 0.85 (Chapter 8)
Holes: mu_min = 54.3, mu_0 = 461.2 cm^2/V.s, N_ref = 2.35e17 cm^-3, alpha = 0.88 (Arora et al. 1982, 300 K)
Phonon terms scaled so the lattice mobility at 300 K has slope -2.42 (electrons) or -2.20 (holes)
limitations: The split between phonon mechanisms is a model; only the total is measured
Extrapolation away from 300 K; underestimates mobility for degenerate doping at low temperature
No freeze-out, screening, neutral impurity, or carrier-carrier scattering
